title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on AI and public standards, outlining its stance on the key issues raised. It highlights commitments to strengthen accountability, transparency, safety and regulatory frameworks for AI systems while encouraging continued research and stakeholder collaboration.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines its plan to oversee and control the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, ensuring that AI tools meet high standards of fairness and integrity. The policy responds to requests from senior education and trade officials, aiming to protect the quality and reliability of qualifications while encouraging responsible AI innovation.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how artificial intelligence systems use copyrighted works during training and the potential legal, economic, and creative impacts of that practice. It evaluates risks and opportunities, proposing guidelines to balance copyright protection with the advancement of AI technologies.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its commitment to strengthen AI regulation and support innovation. It highlights measures to improve safety, transparency, data protection, and investment in AI research while addressing ethical concerns.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence affects public standards. It also includes a set of frequently asked questions to help stakeholders understand the committee’s mandate and process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The CSPL submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on how Artificial Intelligence should be governed. The submission offers the organisation’s views and recommendations on AI policy and regulation.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document explains how artificial intelligence will change the rules that govern medical products, making sure they stay safe and effective. It outlines how to apply the key ideas from the AI White Paper to create clear, consistent regulations for AI‑driven medical devices and treatments.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the defence organization the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user for its size. It sets out a vision for leading in AI capabilities and ensuring responsible, strategic use of technology.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will team up with the transport sector to use AI for better efficiency, safety, and innovation. It also outlines steps to identify and manage any risks that AI could bring to the industry.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how AI developers are using copyrighted works in their systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, summarizing current practices and compliance levels. It highlights progress made, identifies challenges, and recommends actions to better align AI training with copyright law.
